summary: 80-foot steel tower built at Carlin Hill in 1925, moved to Caddell Mountain in Preston County in 1946; registered 2013 and still standing and maintained as of 2017.

events.note: Built at Carlin Hill near Smithfield, Wetzel County, as a state-owned fire tower
Dismantled in summer 1946 at Carlin Hill, moved to Caddell Mountain, and re-erected that fall; the Carlin Hill site was removed from service in 1946
Registered December 12, 2013 as US 979, WV 9; nominated by Ron Stafford
Carlin Hill record says the West Virginia Division of Forestry continued to maintain the relocated tower as of 2017

corrections.proposed: 1925 built at Carlin Hill, Wetzel County; 1946 relocated to Caddell Mountain and re-erected
corrections.why: The NHLR description says the tower was originally at Carlin Hill and was moved and re-erected at Caddell Mountain in 1946. The Carlin Hill record gives the build year as 1925, so 1946 is the move, not the original build.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: NHLR gives 'Built 1946' for the Caddell Mountain entry, while the Carlin Hill record gives 'Built 1925' for the same steel tower before its move. The story uses 1925 for the original build and 1946 for the move and re-erection.
The Carlin Hill record spells the mountain 'Cadell Mountain'; NHLR and Forest Lookouts use 'Caddell Mountain'. The story uses the NHLR spelling.

notes_for_editor: Brief correction: the record's 1946 'built' is the move date; the original build was 1925 at Carlin Hill (firetower.org). Access and visit conditions are not in any source read: the NHLR page has no visit reports, so access is left out of facts. A Facebook group post claims the tower stands 'on private land'; it was not used because it is unverified. A 2019 Dominion Post report says Preston County bought a 0.69-acre parcel near a communications tower on Caddell Mountain; it does not say whether the fire lookout sits on that land, so it is not used. The Carlin Hill record is the only source for the 1925 build and the 2017 maintenance statement; the 'as of 2017' date is from that page and no later status was found. The brief's 'standing' status is supported by the FFLOS list and the 2017 maintenance note, but the current condition is not confirmed. The brief's 914.1 m elevation matches NHLR's 914 m rounding.
